criteria.title: Two threads share one process mapping but own execution frames; one exits while the other is blocked.
criteria.task: Two threads share one process mapping but own execution frames; one exits while the other is blocked.
criteria.purpose: Assess this particular ownership, state, ordering, resource or evidence boundary independently.

knowledge: T56.01 teaching and full parent contract
C17 object lifetime, integer bounds, caller/target ownership and declared machine model
artifacts: PR-T56-01 learner source/analysis and precise reused-component identities; absent required implementations remain work

reasoning: Two threads share one process mapping but own execution frames; one exits while the other is blocked.
Derive: Thread exit alone does not release the process address space while another live thread remains. Each TCB owns a saved frame and stack; process resources have a different lifetime.
State pre/postconditions, invariants, resource costs, failure publication and exact evidence limits. Separate ISO C, original model, compiler/ABI, ISA/OS and physical premises.

deliverables.D2: Implementation or inspectable analysis with source identities: Actual separate process/TCB pools, per-thread frames, quiescent reaping and four-thread guest tests. Address this remaining obligation: Expanded cancellation/reference accounting and independent process/thread identity assessment remain required.
deliverables.D3: Independent expectation, fresh counterexample and first-divergence evidence: Thread exit alone does not release the process address space while another live thread remains. Each TCB owns a saved frame and stack; process resources have a different lifetime.
deliverables.D4: After at least7days independently attempt: Terminate the process while one thread runs remotely and prove no frame reuse until every CPU leaves.
